mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines seasonal unemployment as described for industrial workers during the Age of Industrialisation?

options.A: Unemployment that occurs when workers are laid off because demand for their labour falls during certain seasons
options.B: Unemployment caused by a permanent lack of skills among workers
options.C: Unemployment that lasts for the entire working life of a person
options.D: Unemployment that results from the introduction of new machinery

mcqs.answer: Unemployment that occurs when workers are laid off because demand for their labour falls during certain seasons
mcqs.explanation: Seasonal unemployment refers to temporary job loss that happens at particular times of the year when the demand for certain types of work drops, such as agricultural or textile work during off‑season periods. It is distinct from structural (skill‑mismatch) or cyclical (economy‑wide) unemployment. Options B, C and D describe other types of unemployment.

mcqs.question: Which of the following actions best illustrates the resistance shown by industrial workers against poor working conditions in the 19th‑century factories?

options.A: Forming trade unions and organising strikes
options.C: Moving back to villages to take up agriculture

mcqs.answer: Forming trade unions and organising strikes
mcqs.explanation: Workers resisted exploitation mainly by coming together to form trade unions and by staging strikes, which forced factory owners to negotiate better wages and working hours. The other options describe passive or opposite behaviours, not resistance.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the impact of industrialisation on urban life
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of how industrialisation changed urban life in India during the Age of Industrialisation?

options.A: The rapid growth of crowded slums near factories
options.B: A steady decline in the population of major towns
options.C: A revival of traditional hand‑loom weaving as the main occupation
options.D: A significant reduction in air and water pollution in cities

mcqs.answer: The rapid growth of crowded slums near factories
mcqs.explanation: Industrialisation attracted large numbers of workers to cities, leading to the emergence of densely populated slums with inadequate housing and sanitation. Options B, C and D are contrary to the historical impact of industrialisation.

mcqs.question: A factory supervisor tells workers that they must work from 6 am to 8 pm with only a 30‑minute break for lunch. Which condition does this scenario best illustrate?

options.A: Long working hours with minimal breaks
options.B: Flexible working hours allowing workers to choose their shifts
options.C: High wages and a safe, well‑ventilated work environment
options.D: The possibility of working from home

mcqs.answer: Long working hours with minimal breaks
mcqs.explanation: The description highlights excessive daily hours and a very short lunch break, typical of the harsh factory conditions faced by many industrial workers. The other options do not match the scenario.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify problems of wages and employment
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is a common misconception about the wages and employment of factory workers during the early phase of industrialisation?

options.A: All factory workers earned wages sufficient for a decent standard of living
options.B: Many workers received irregular or very low wages
options.C: Employment in factories was often insecure and temporary
options.D: Child labour was widely employed in factories

mcqs.answer: All factory workers earned wages sufficient for a decent standard of living
mcqs.explanation: The belief that every factory worker earned a decent wage is incorrect; most earned meagre, irregular wages that barely met basic needs. Options B, C and D correctly describe the hardships faced by workers.

mcqs.question: A textile mill in a region that receives heavy monsoon rains shuts down its production for three months each year. The workers who lose their jobs during this period are experiencing which type of unemployment?
mcqs.explanation: The shutdown is tied to a predictable seasonal factor (monsoon), so the resulting job loss is seasonal unemployment. Structural unemployment arises from skill mismatches, frictional from job search transitions, and cyclical from overall economic downturns.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares two common forms of resistance used by industrial workers in the 19th century?

options.A: Strikes involve a collective stoppage of work, whereas sabotage involves damaging machinery or tools to disrupt production
options.B: Both strikes and sabotage were always illegal and never led to any negotiation with employers
options.C: Sabotage was a peaceful form of protest, while strikes always turned violent
options.D: Strikes were individual actions taken by a single worker, whereas sabotage required the whole workforce

mcqs.answer: Strikes involve a collective stoppage of work, whereas sabotage involves damaging machinery or tools to disrupt production
mcqs.explanation: Strikes are organized work stoppages by groups of workers to demand better conditions. Sabotage, on the other hand, is the deliberate damage of equipment to hinder production. Options B, C and D misrepresent the nature and legality of these actions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the impact of industrialisation on urban life
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the impact of industrialisation on urban life in India is NOT correct?

options.A: It led to the growth of well‑planned residential colonies for all workers
options.B: It caused overcrowding and inadequate sanitation in many towns
options.C: It created new employment opportunities in factories and related services
options.D: It resulted in the emergence of a wage‑labour class

mcqs.answer: It led to the growth of well‑planned residential colonies for all workers
mcqs.explanation: Industrialisation largely produced haphazard, poorly planned settlements for workers, not well‑planned colonies for everyone. Overcrowding, sanitation problems, new jobs, and a wage‑labour class (options B, C, D) were genuine impacts.
